intent.raw_query: Portugal Algarve, $2200, beach holiday with wine tasting, September 2026 from London

selected_hotel.name: Praia da Marinha, Lagoa Boutique Stay

experiences.name: Praia da Marinha Coastal Hike & Swim
experiences.description: Explore one of the Algarve's most stunning beaches, Praia da Marinha, known for its dramatic golden limestone cliffs, sea caves, and crystal-clear turquoise waters. Hike the clifftop trail for panoramic views, then descend to the secluded cove for a swim among the rock formations.

experiences.name: Algarve Wine & Vineyard Tour
experiences.description: Visit local Algarve wineries such as Quinta dos Vales or Adega do Cantor near Guia, sampling regional varietals including Negra Mole and Arinto. Guided tours include barrel tastings, vineyard walks, and food pairings with local cheeses and charcuterie, offering a deep dive into the region's emerging wine scene.

experiences.name: Benagil Sea Cave Kayak Tour
experiences.description: Paddle by kayak from Praia de Benagil into the famous Algar de Benagil sea cave, one of the most iconic natural wonders of the Algarve. A guided kayak tour lets you explore hidden grottos, arched rock formations, and a secret interior beach illuminated by a natural skylight.

experiences.name: Sagres Sunset & Cabo de São Vicente Visit
experiences.description: Travel to the southwestern tip of Europe at Cabo de São Vicente and the historic Sagres Fortress. Watch the dramatic Atlantic sunset from the cliffs, explore the fortress walls steeped in Age of Discovery history, and enjoy the wild, windswept beauty of this UNESCO-recognized landscape.

experiences.name: Ria Formosa Natural Park Boat Tour & Seafood Lunch
experiences.description: Take a guided boat tour through the Ria Formosa lagoon system, a protected natural park teeming with flamingos, herons, and migratory birds. Stop at barrier islands like Ilha Deserta for a pristine beach experience, then enjoy a fresh seafood lunch featuring local clams, grilled fish, and regional white wine at a waterfront restaurant.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Portugal Algarve
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

hotel.name: Praia da Marinha, Lagoa Boutique Stay

day_by_day.morning: Flight arrives at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Collect luggage, arrange transfer or rent a budget car at Faro Airport (pre-book online for best rates ~€25-35/day). Drive ~45 min west to Praia da Marinha, Lagoa Boutique Stay and check in.
day_by_day.afternoon: After settling in, take a short 10-minute walk down the cliff path to Praia da Marinha — consistently rated one of Portugal's most beautiful beaches. Explore the golden limestone rock arches, sea caves, and crystal-clear turquoise water. Swim and decompress after the flight. Entry is free.
day_by_day.evening: Head into nearby Carvoeiro village (10 min drive) for your first taste of the Algarve. Stroll the small beach promenade and browse the local shops. Grab a light dinner at a casual esplanade restaurant along the waterfront.

meals.breakfast: Grab a pastel de nata and coffee at the airport before or after landing (~€2-3)
meals.lunch: Pick up snacks from a local mini-market or petrol station on the drive from Faro (~€5)
meals.dinner: O Castelo in Carvoeiro — a budget-friendly local restaurant with grilled fish of the day (peixe do dia) and house wine. Expect €12-16 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Pre-book your rental car online before travel for the best budget rates. Download the Via Verde app if driving on Portuguese toll roads. The cliff path to Praia da Marinha can be steep — wear comfortable shoes.

day_by_day.morning: Start with a leisurely breakfast then explore the Algar Seco rock formations in Carvoeiro — a dramatic coastal area with grottos, arches, and natural pools carved by the sea. Walk the free boardwalk trail along the cliffs (about 1.5 km). Arrive early to beat any crowds.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive 15 minutes west to Praia de Benagil. Take a short kayak or stand-up paddleboard rental (~€15/hr) or join a budget boat tour (~€15-20) to enter the famous Benagil Cave — one of the Algarve's most iconic sea caves with a natural skylight. Book tours locally at the beach.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the Lagoa area and visit the small town of Lagoa itself. Walk the quiet streets, visit Igreja Matriz de Lagoa (free), and find a local tasca (tavern) for dinner.

meals.breakfast: Café Bonança in Carvoeiro — coffee and toast with local butter and jam (tosta mista ~€3.50)
meals.lunch: Pack sandwiches from a local padaria (bakery) in Carvoeiro (~€3-4) and eat at Benagil beach
meals.dinner: Tasca do Lagoa in Lagoa town — hearty Portuguese home cooking, cataplana de marisco (seafood stew) shared between two, house wine carafe. ~€13-15 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Benagil Cave boat tours sell out fast even in September. Book the morning before or as soon as you arrive at the beach. Swimming into the cave is not recommended and sometimes restricted — the boat tour is worth the small cost.

day_by_day.morning: Wine tasting morning! Drive 10 minutes to Adega do Cantor (Cliff Richard's famous winery) near Guia or alternatively visit Quinta dos Vales near Estômbar (~20 min). Quinta dos Vales offers affordable guided vineyard tours and tastings starting from ~€10-15 per person. Learn about Algarve's unique Negra Mole and Castelão grape varieties.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the winery, head to Praia de Armação de Pêra (~20 min drive) — one of the longest beaches in the Algarve with calm, shallow waters perfect for swimming. Relax on the wide sandy beach. Beach access is free.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Armação de Pêra's seafront promenade and small fishing village area. Watch local fishermen bring in their catch near the old fort chapel (Igreja de Nossa Senhora do Mar).

meals.breakfast: At the accommodation or a nearby café — galão (milky coffee) and croissant (~€3)
meals.lunch: Light snack at the winery if included in tour, or grab a bifana (pork roll) from a roadside café (~€2.50)
meals.dinner: Restaurante Zé Leiteiro in Armação de Pêra — beloved local spot, grilled sea bass or sardines with potatoes and salad. ~€12-14 per person including a glass of wine.

day_by_day.notes: Call ahead to confirm winery tour times and book a spot — September is harvest season so wineries may be busy but also very atmospheric. Quinta dos Vales is particularly scenic and budget-friendly.

day_by_day.morning: Drive ~35 minutes west to Silves — the ancient Moorish capital of the Algarve. Visit the spectacular red sandstone Castelo de Silves (€3 entry, one of Portugal's best-preserved Moorish castles). Explore the ramparts with panoramic views over orange groves and the Arade River.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk down to the Gothic Sé Catedral de Silves (€1.30 entry) and explore the charming cobblestone streets of this underrated historic town. Visit the small Museu Arqueológico (€2) to learn about the region's Roman and Moorish history. Browse the local market if it's running.
day_by_day.evening: Stay in Silves for dinner — it's a great spot for authentic, non-touristy food. Walk along the Arade River at sunset.

meals.breakfast: At accommodation or a café near Lagoa before departure
meals.lunch: Café Inglês in Silves — a quirky café inside the castle walls with affordable sandwiches, soups, and local specials (~€8-10)
meals.dinner: Marisqueira Rui in Silves — a legendary local seafood restaurant, famous for affordable grilled fish platters and cold Sagres beer. ~€14-18 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Silves is dramatically less touristy and cheaper than Lagos or Albufeira. September is a great time to visit as the town hosts its famous Medieval Fair (usually August — check if any events extend). The castle and cathedral together take about 2-3 hours.

day_by_day.morning: Beach day at Praia da Marinha — your home beach. Spend the morning exploring the hidden coves and sea caves accessible by walking the coastal trail from the main beach. Bring snorkeling gear (cheap sets available at local shops ~€10-15) to explore the rich marine life in the crystal-clear rock pools.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive 5 minutes to Praia de Albandeira — a tiny, secluded gem of a beach framed by dramatic rock formations. Much quieter than Marinha, with a natural stone arch. Perfect for a peaceful afternoon swim.
day_by_day.evening: Visit Ferragudo village (~20 min drive) — one of the most picturesque fishing villages in the Algarve. Walk up to Castelo de São João do Arade (exterior free) for sunset views over the Arade estuary and Portimão across the water.

meals.breakfast: Self-catering at accommodation — pick up fresh bread, local cheese, ham, and fruit from a local supermarket the day before (~€8-10 for supplies)
meals.lunch: Picnic on the beach — fresh fruit, local bread, and cheese from the supermarket
meals.dinner: A Lanterna in Ferragudo — a charming riverside restaurant with excellent grilled fish, very popular with locals. Book ahead for weekends. ~€15-18 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Saturday can get busy at popular beaches even in September. Arrive at Praia da Marinha before 10am for the best parking and quietest experience. Ferragudo is a wonderful alternative to the more commercial Portimão and worth the short drive.

day_by_day.morning: Drive ~40 minutes west to Lagos — one of the Algarve's most beloved towns. Start with a walk through the historic old town, visiting the Mercado de Escravos (Slave Market Museum, €3) — a sobering but historically important site. Explore the beautifully tiled Igreja de Santo António (€3, includes town museum).
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk the famous Ponta da Piedade coastal trail (~3 km round trip, free) — a stunning series of golden limestone sea stacks, arches, and grottos. Hire a kayak or small boat from the bottom of the cliffs to explore sea caves (~€15-20). The views from the cliff tops are equally spectacular and free.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Lagos' vibrant Rua 25 de Abril for bars and restaurants. The town has a youthful, lively atmosphere on Sunday evenings. Enjoy a sundowner at a cliff-top bar.

meals.breakfast: Stop at a pastelaria in Lagos old town — coffee and pastel de nata (~€2)
meals.lunch: : Mercado Municipal de Lagos food hall — fresh, affordable local food stalls with fish, meat, and vegetarian options. ~€8-10
meals.dinner: O Camilo in Lagos (near Praia do Camilo) — rustic, affordable seafood with stunning cliff views. Grilled fish or seafood rice. ~€14-16 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Lagos is about 40 minutes from your accommodation — plan to spend the full day. Ponta da Piedade is best visited in the afternoon when the sun illuminates the rock formations from the west. Parking in Lagos can be tricky on Sundays — use the free parking near the train station and walk in.

day_by_day.morning: Drive ~55 minutes west to Sagres — the southwestern tip of Portugal and of continental Europe. Visit the dramatic Fortaleza de Sagres (€3) perched on the clifftop promontory. Explore the mysterious wind compass (Rosa dos Ventos) and learn about Henry the Navigator's role in the Age of Exploration.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk 10 minutes to Cabo de São Vicente — the most southwestern point of continental Europe. Stand on the wild, windswept cliffs above crashing Atlantic waves. The lighthouse is free to visit externally; a small museum inside costs €3. Buy local honey or smoked sausages from the small market vendors.
day_by_day.evening: Drive back east, stopping in Portimão (~30 min from Sagres, ~20 min from your hotel) for dinner. Portimão is famous for its grilled sardines and lively riverfront.

meals.breakfast: Pack breakfast from accommodation or stop at a café in Portimão on the way through
meals.lunch: Snack bar near Sagres fortress or bring a packed lunch — options in Sagres are limited and can be pricey. Budget €5-8.
meals.dinner: Tasca da Barca in Portimão — a tiny, authentic local restaurant on the riverfront famous for chargrilled sardines (sardinhas assadas). One of the best budget meals in the Algarve. ~€10-13 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Sagres and Cabo de São Vicente are noticeably windier and cooler than the rest of the Algarve — bring a light jacket. The drive west on the N125 is scenic. September is a great time as summer crowds have thinned. Sardine season runs June-October so September is still excellent for fresh sardines.

day_by_day.morning: Second wine tasting experience! Visit Adega Cooperativa de Lagoa — the local cooperative winery right in Lagoa town (~10 min drive). This is one of the most affordable wine experiences in the Algarve, with tastings from as little as €5-8. Buy bottles of local wine to take home at excellent prices (€4-8/bottle).
day_by_day.afternoon: Spend the afternoon at Praia de Carvoeiro — the main beach of Carvoeiro village, a small, picturesque horseshoe-shaped cove framed by golden cliffs. Swim, sunbathe, and people-watch. Walk the clifftop boardwalk (Passadiço de Carvoeiro) for scenic views.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Carvoeiro village in the early evening — browse local craft shops, watch the sunset from the clifftops, and enjoy the relaxed village atmosphere.

meals.breakfast: Padaria local bakery near accommodation — fresh bread rolls, butter, and coffee (~€3)
meals.lunch: Snack bar on Praia de Carvoeiro — prego no pão (steak sandwich) or tosta mista (~€5-7)
meals.dinner: Restaurante O Pátio in Carvoeiro — a local favorite with a shaded courtyard, serving traditional cataplana and grilled fish at reasonable prices. ~€13-16 per person.

day_by_day.notes: The Adega Cooperativa de Lagoa is a hidden gem — locals buy their wine here year-round. You can purchase wine by the bottle or even the 5-liter bag-in-box for exceptional value. The cooperative wines are genuinely excellent and underrated.

day_by_day.morning: Drive ~1 hour east to Faro — the Algarve's capital and a beautifully underrated city. Start in the Cidade Velha (Old Town), entering through the grand Arco da Vila. Visit the Sé Catedral de Faro (€3.50, climb the tower for panoramic views) and the eerie but fascinating Igreja dos Ossos (Bone Chapel, €4) inside the Carmo Church.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a short ferry (~€2.50 return) from Faro harbor to Ilha Deserta (Desert Island) or Ilha de Faro — pristine barrier islands within the Ria Formosa Natural Park. Enjoy some of the most unspoiled beaches in the Algarve with calm lagoon water on one side and Atlantic surf on the other.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Faro for dinner in the lively Baixa (downtown) area before driving back to Lagoa (~1 hour).

meals.breakfast: At accommodation before departure
meals.lunch: Bar Restaurante on Ilha Deserta — fresh grilled fish with a view. Slightly pricier due to location but worth it for the experience. ~€14-16. Alternatively pack a lunch.
meals.dinner: Faz Gostos in Faro old town — excellent traditional Algarvian cuisine in a beautiful historic building at moderate prices. ~€14-17 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Faro is often skipped by tourists who fly straight to beach resorts — don't make this mistake! The Ria Formosa Natural Park is a UNESCO-listed biosphere reserve. Check ferry times at the Faro harbor before heading to the islands — last ferries back are typically late afternoon.

day_by_day.morning: Relaxed morning at Praia da Marinha. Take the longer coastal hiking trail (Percurso dos Sete Vales Suspensos — Seven Hanging Valleys Trail, ~6 km one way) which starts near Praia de Vale de Centeanes and ends near Praia da Marinha. This is one of the most spectacular coastal walks in Europe and completely free.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the hike, cool off with a swim at whichever cove you finish near. Visit a local fish market in Portimão (~20 min drive) if timing aligns — the Mercado Municipal has fresh local produce at great prices.
day_by_day.evening: Cook a simple dinner at the accommodation using fresh market produce — fresh fish, local vegetables, and a bottle of wine from the Lagoa cooperative. A great budget evening.

meals.breakfast: Self-catering — yogurt, local fruit, bread and coffee at accommodation
meals.lunch: Pack a picnic for the trail — local bread, cheese, fruit, and water (essential on this hike)
meals.dinner: Self-catering at accommodation — fresh fish from the market grilled simply with local olive oil, garlic, and lemon. A bottle of Lagoa cooperative wine. Total ~€10-12 for two people.

day_by_day.notes: The Seven Hanging Valleys Trail is best done west to east (ending at Praia da Marinha near your hotel). Wear proper walking shoes — the path is rocky in places. Bring at least 1.5 liters of water per person and sun protection. The trail is moderate difficulty and takes 2-3 hours.

day_by_day.morning: Drive ~50 minutes east to Tavira — arguably the most beautiful town in the Algarve and one of the most undervisited. Cross the Roman bridge over the Gilão River, visit the ruins of the Moorish Castelo de Tavira (free), and explore the 37 churches (Igreja de Santa Maria do Castelo has beautiful azulejo tiles).
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a short ferry (~€1.60 return) from Quatro Águas dock to Ilha de Tavira — a stunning barrier island with kilometers of pristine beach within the Ria Formosa. The water here is exceptionally calm and clear. Spend the afternoon swimming and relaxing.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Tavira town for a sunset stroll and dinner before driving back.

meals.breakfast: Stop at a café in Tavira — the town has excellent traditional pastelarias
meals.lunch: Pack snacks for the island beach or use the small seasonal kiosk on Ilha de Tavira
meals.dinner: Restaurante Bica in Tavira — a beloved local institution serving fresh Ria Formosa clams (amêijoas à Bulhão Pato), grilled fish, and local wines at very fair prices. ~€13-16 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Tavira is about 1 hour east of your accommodation — make a full day of it. The town has a distinctly different, more refined character than the western Algarve. September is a beautiful time as the summer rush has ended but weather remains warm. The Ria Formosa clams in Tavira are among the best in Portugal.

day_by_day.morning: Final full beach day — revisit your favorite beach (Praia da Marinha recommended) or try Praia do Carvalho (~5 min drive) — a tiny, secluded cove accessible through a tunnel carved in the cliff. One of the most dramatic and hidden beaches in the Algarve. Arrive early as it's small and fills up.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Portimão for some last-minute souvenir shopping at the Mercado Municipal and along Rua Direita. Pick up local products: medronho (arbutus berry brandy, ~€8-12/bottle), local honey, almond sweets (Dom Rodrigos), dried figs, and local wine. These make excellent budget gifts.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner — splurge slightly on your last night in the Algarve. Head to Ferragudo or Carvoeiro for a special meal to celebrate the trip.

meals.breakfast: Leisurely breakfast at a café in Carvoeiro — full Portuguese breakfast with eggs, ham, cheese, toast, and coffee (~€6-8)
meals.lunch: Light lunch at a beachside snack bar — fresh grilled prawns or a prego sandwich (~€8-10)
meals.dinner: Restaurante Sueste in Ferragudo — a well-regarded local restaurant with fresh seafood, excellent cataplana, and a lovely terrace. Treat yourself to a slightly nicer bottle of local wine. ~€18-22 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Praia do Carvalho is accessed via a narrow tunnel — it's very easy to miss the entrance (look for a small gap in the cliff face on the coastal path). The tunnel is about 50m long and unlit, so a phone torch helps. The beach inside is magical and worth the effort.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning — take one last walk down to Praia da Marinha for a sunrise or early morning swim. Pack up your bags and check out of the accommodation. Allow time to clean the space and do a final check for belongings.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive to Faro Airport (~45 min). Return the rental car — allow at least 30-45 minutes for the return process and airport check-in. Grab a final coffee and pastel de nata at the airport.
day_by_day.evening: Depart from Faro Airport. Carry home memories of golden cliffs, turquoise coves, local wine, fresh sardines, and the warm Algarvian sun.

meals.breakfast: Final breakfast at the accommodation — use up any remaining groceries or stop at a café in Lagoa for a last galão and tosta
meals.lunch: Airport café or restaurant — budget €10-15 for a light meal before departure
meals.dinner: On the flight or at your destination

day_by_day.notes: Check flight departure time carefully and plan your drive to Faro accordingly. The A22 toll road is the fastest route — use a credit card at toll booths or ensure your rental car has Via Verde. Return the rental car at least 2 hours before departure. Don't forget to declare any wine, honey, or food products if returning to a non-EU country.

trip_options.title: Classic Portugal Algarve Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

hotel.name: Praia da Marinha, Lagoa Boutique Stay

day_by_day.morning: Flight arrival – no activities scheduled before 13:00
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Faro Airport at 13:00. Collect luggage and pick up a pre-booked rental car (essential for the Algarve). Drive approximately 45 minutes west to Praia da Marinha, Lagoa Boutique Stay. Check in, freshen up, and take a leisurely first stroll along the clifftop path above Praia da Marinha to soak in the dramatic limestone rock formations and turquoise water.
day_by_day.evening: Head into the nearby village of Carvoeiro (10 min drive) for a relaxed first dinner. Explore the charming main square and beachfront strip before settling in for the night.

meals.breakfast: On the plane
meals.lunch: Grab a quick bite at the airport or a roadside café en route (try a bifana sandwich and coffee – under €5)
meals.dinner: Restaurante O Castelo in Carvoeiro – traditional Portuguese dishes like grilled sea bass and cataplana de marisco; mid-range, around €20–28 per person

day_by_day.notes: Pick up a Portuguese SIM card at the airport for data. Pre-book your rental car to avoid queues. September is an excellent month – warm (26–28°C), sea still very swimmable, crowds thinning after peak summer.

day_by_day.morning: After breakfast at the boutique stay, walk or drive the 2-minute path down to Praia da Marinha itself – consistently ranked one of Portugal's most beautiful beaches. Spend the morning swimming in the crystal-clear coves, snorkelling around the sea arches, and exploring the rock pools.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive 15 minutes west to Algar Seco, a spectacular coastal rock formation near Carvoeiro. Walk the short boardwalk trail through the eroded limestone pillars and sea caves. Afterwards, stop at Praia de Benagil to see the famous Benagil Sea Cave from the beach (book a kayak or small boat tour in advance to enter the cave – tours run ~€15–20 per person).
day_by_day.evening: Return to Carvoeiro village for sunset drinks at a clifftop bar, then dinner in the village.

meals.breakfast: At the boutique stay or a local pastelaria – pastéis de nata, fresh orange juice, galão coffee
meals.lunch: O Boneco beach bar near Benagil – fresh grilled fish, salads; budget ~€14–18
meals.dinner: Restaurante Boneca in Carvoeiro – try the açorda de marisco (seafood bread stew) or grilled dourada; ~€22–30 per person

day_by_day.notes: Book the Benagil Cave boat tour the evening before as September spots still fill quickly. Wear water shoes for rock pool exploration at Marinha.

day_by_day.morning: Drive 20 minutes east to Lagoa town to visit the Lagoa Wine Cooperative (Adega Cooperativa de Lagoa) – one of the oldest and most respected wine producers in the Algarve. Join a guided cellar tour and tasting of their local Algarve DOC wines, including the distinctive red and white varieties made from Negra Mole and Arinto grapes.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue east to the historic town of Silves (15 min drive). Visit the impressive red sandstone Silves Castle (Castelo de Silves), the former Moorish capital of the Algarve. Explore the Medieval Cathedral of Silves and wander the cobblestone streets of the old town.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy dinner in Silves before returning to the hotel.

meals.breakfast: At the boutique stay
meals.lunch: Café Inglês in Silves – charming terrace restaurant with views of the castle, serving local cuisine; ~€15–20
meals.dinner: Restaurante Marisqueira Rui in Silves – famous for seafood and cataplana; a local institution; ~€25–35 per person

day_by_day.notes: The Lagoa Wine Cooperative requires advance booking for tours – call or email ahead. Silves Castle entry is approximately €3. Silves is a quieter, authentic alternative to the coastal tourist spots.

day_by_day.morning: Drive 35 minutes west to Portimão and take a boat trip along the Arade River or along the western Algarve coastline. Alternatively, visit Praia da Rocha, one of the most famous Algarve beaches, with its wide golden sands and towering ochre cliffs. Walk the clifftop promenade and explore the 16th-century Fortress of Santa Catarina.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head into Portimão town centre. Visit the Museu de Portimão (free on Sundays, ~€3 other days) – a fascinating museum housed in a converted sardine canning factory, telling the story of the region's fishing heritage. Browse the riverside market stalls.
day_by_day.evening: Stay in Portimão for dinner – the town is famous for its grilled sardines and riverside fish restaurants.

meals.breakfast: At the boutique stay
meals.lunch: A riverside tasca in Portimão – grilled sardines with boiled potatoes and salad, the quintessential Algarve lunch; ~€10–15
meals.dinner: Taberna da Maré in Portimão – excellent seafood in a relaxed setting; ~€20–28 per person with wine

day_by_day.notes: Portimão hosts a famous International Sardine Festival in August, but September still offers great sardine grilling at local tascas. The Museu de Portimão is genuinely excellent and often overlooked by tourists.

day_by_day.morning: Drive 50 minutes west to explore the dramatic landscapes of the Costa Vicentina – the wild, unspoiled Atlantic coast. Visit Praia da Arrifana, a stunning surf beach set below towering cliffs with a ruined Moorish fort. Alternatively, visit Praia do Amado, one of the Algarve's top surf beaches.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue north to the village of Aljezur – a charming hilltop village with a Moorish castle ruin and a relaxed, bohemian atmosphere. Explore the castle grounds, the small local market (Saturday market is active), and the old Moorish quarter.
day_by_day.evening: Drive back east (about 55 minutes) to your hotel. Opt for a quiet dinner near Carvoeiro or cook in if the boutique stay has facilities.

meals.breakfast: At the boutique stay – pack snacks for the road trip
meals.lunch: Restaurante Arrifana or a local surf café near Praia do Amado – fresh fish, salads, smoothies; ~€12–18
meals.dinner: A Ruína restaurant near Carvoeiro or a local tasca in Lagoa – simple grilled meats or fish; ~€18–24

day_by_day.notes: The Costa Vicentina is part of the Southwest Alentejo and Vicentine Coast Natural Park – one of Europe's last wild coastlines. Wear layers as the Atlantic side can be windier and slightly cooler. Check surf conditions if you want to try surfing – Amado has a surf school.

day_by_day.morning: Relaxed morning at Praia da Marinha or nearby Praia de Albandeira (a quieter, equally beautiful cove just 5 minutes away). Swim, read, and recharge. This is a deliberately slower day after yesterday's long drive.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive 20 minutes to Ferragudo – a beautifully preserved fishing village on the mouth of the Arade River, largely untouched by mass tourism. Explore the whitewashed streets, the 16th-century Castelo de São João de Arade, and the small fishing harbour. Take a short ferry across the river to Portimão if desired.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset walk along Ferragudo's waterfront, then dinner in the village.

meals.breakfast: At the boutique stay – leisurely Sunday breakfast
meals.lunch: Picnic on the beach – pick up local bread, cheese, presunto (cured ham), olives, and local wine from a Lagoa supermarket or deli the evening before
meals.dinner: Restaurante Sueste in Ferragudo – outstanding seafood with river and sea views; one of the best restaurants in the central Algarve; ~€28–38 per person

day_by_day.notes: Ferragudo is a hidden gem – far less commercialised than Carvoeiro or Lagos. Sunday is ideal for a slow morning. Sueste is popular; book ahead even in September.

day_by_day.morning: Drive 1 hour east to Faro, the Algarve's capital city. Begin with a visit to the Cidade Velha (Old Town) – enter through the 18th-century Arco da Vila and explore the cathedral (Sé de Faro), the Bishop's Palace, and the charming pedestrian streets. Climb the cathedral tower for panoramic views over the Ria Formosa lagoon.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Museu Municipal de Faro (housed in a former convent) and the hauntingly beautiful Igreja dos Ossos (Chapel of Bones) in the Igreja de Nossa Senhora do Carmo. Then take a short ferry from Faro's pier to the Ilha Deserta (Desert Island) – a pristine, car-free barrier island with a long sandy beach and crystal lagoon water.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Faro for dinner in the lively Baixa (downtown) area before driving back to the hotel.

meals.breakfast: At the boutique stay
meals.lunch: Restaurante 2 Irmãos in Faro – a Faro institution since 1925, serving traditional Algarve cuisine; ~€18–25
meals.dinner: Tasca do Ricky in Faro – cosy, authentic, excellent value petiscos (Portuguese tapas) and daily specials; ~€15–22 per person

day_by_day.notes: Ilha Deserta ferries run regularly from Faro pier (€8–10 return). The island has one excellent but pricey restaurant – bring your own water and snacks if on a budget. Faro's old town is compact and very walkable.

day_by_day.morning: Drive 1 hour east to Tavira – widely considered the most beautiful and authentic town in the Algarve. Cross the Roman bridge over the Gilão River, visit the Castle of Tavira for panoramic views, and explore the Igreja de Santa Maria do Castelo. Wander the tile-fronted streets and admire the distinctive four-sided scissor rooftops unique to Tavira.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take the ferry from Quatro Águas pier (just outside Tavira) to Ilha de Tavira – a stunning barrier island beach that stretches for kilometres with calm lagoon water on one side and Atlantic waves on the other. Spend the afternoon swimming and relaxing.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Tavira for dinner and an evening stroll along the river before driving back west.

meals.breakfast: Stop at a pastelaria in Tavira – try the local Dom Rodrigo almond sweets
meals.lunch: Beach bar on Ilha de Tavira – fresh grilled fish or salads; ~€14–20
meals.dinner: Restaurante Bica in Tavira – beloved local restaurant, excellent cataplana and fresh fish; ~€22–30 per person

day_by_day.notes: Tavira is the cultural highlight of the eastern Algarve. The island beach is quieter by mid-September – a real treat. Ferry to Ilha de Tavira costs ~€2.50 return. Allow extra time for the drive back (1 hour to Lagoa).

day_by_day.morning: Dedicated wine day. Drive 25 minutes north into the Algarve interior to visit Quinta dos Vales, a boutique winery near Estômbar with impressive sculpture gardens and excellent wine. Book a guided vineyard tour and tasting of their award-winning reds, whites, and rosés – the Algarve's warm climate produces surprisingly bold wines.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue to a second winery: Quinta da Penina or Adega do Cantor (Sir Cliff Richard's winery near Guia) – both offer tastings and are within 20–30 minutes of each other. Purchase a few bottles to take home. Afterwards, explore the rural Algarve countryside – orange groves, carob trees, and rolling hills.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the hotel for a relaxed evening. Open one of your purchased bottles on the terrace at sunset.

meals.breakfast: At the boutique stay
meals.lunch: Light lunch at Quinta dos Vales or a rural café in Estômbar – charcuterie, local cheese, bread paired with wine; ~€12–18
meals.dinner: Restaurante O Leão in Lagoa town – unpretentious local favourite, excellent grilled meats and fish; ~€18–24 per person

day_by_day.notes: Book winery tours in advance – Quinta dos Vales is particularly popular. Adega do Cantor (Cliff Richard's winery) produces the 'Vida Nova' label and tours are well-organised. Consider buying local medronho (arbutus berry spirit) as a unique souvenir.

day_by_day.morning: Drive 45 minutes west to Lagos – the most historically significant and lively town in the western Algarve. Visit the Museu de Lagos (one of the best regional museums in Portugal), the Igreja de Santo António with its extraordinary gilded baroque interior, and the old slave market building (Mercado de Escravos) – the first in Europe.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Lagos's coastline: walk or drive to Ponta da Piedade – a spectacular headland of golden sea stacks, arches, and grottoes. Take a small boat tour from the Lagos marina into the caves and grottos (~€15–20, 45 minutes). Afterwards, relax at Praia Dona Ana or Praia do Camilo – two of the most scenic small beaches in the Algarve.
day_by_day.evening: Stay in Lagos for dinner – the town has an excellent and varied restaurant scene.

meals.breakfast: At the boutique stay
meals.lunch: O Camilo restaurant above Praia do Camilo – stunning views, fresh fish and seafood; ~€22–30
meals.dinner: Adega da Marina in Lagos – rustic, lively, great value traditional food; ~€18–25 per person with wine

day_by_day.notes: Lagos can be busy even in September but is worth it. Ponta da Piedade is best in morning or late afternoon light for photography. Book the grotto boat tour from the marina kiosk when you arrive.

day_by_day.morning: Drive 30 minutes west to Sagres – the dramatic, windswept southwestern tip of Portugal and the end of the known world in the Age of Discovery. Visit the Fortaleza de Sagres, a vast clifftop fortress where Henry the Navigator established his famous school of navigation in the 15th century. Walk the clifftops of Cabo de São Vicente – the most southwesterly point of mainland Europe – and watch the powerful Atlantic swells crash against the cliffs.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return east along the coast, stopping at Praia do Martinhal (a calm, sheltered bay near Sagres, great for families and swimming) or Praia da Ingrina. Take a slower, scenic route back through the Serra de Monchique foothills.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner near Carvoeiro or at the hotel if catering is available.

meals.breakfast: Pack breakfast to eat at Cabo de São Vicente – coffee from a thermos and pastries from a local bakery
meals.lunch: Restaurante O Telheiro do Infante near Sagres – excellent fresh fish with ocean views; ~€20–28
meals.dinner: Restaurante Escondidinho in Carvoeiro – cosy, good-value Portuguese classics; ~€18–24 per person

day_by_day.notes: Cabo de São Vicente is notoriously windy – bring a light jacket even in September. The lighthouse sells a small souvenir stamp for passports/travel journals. Sagres is 1 hour 10 minutes from the hotel so start early.

day_by_day.morning: Drive 30 minutes north into the Serra de Monchique mountains – a lush, forested range that feels worlds apart from the coastal Algarve. Visit the spa town of Caldas de Monchique, a beautiful valley village with thermal springs, plane trees, and 19th-century charm. Try the famous Monchique mineral water at source.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue up to the town of Monchique itself – explore the ruins of the Franciscan convent, browse local craft shops selling medronho spirit and Monchique folding knives (canivetes), and try the local smoked sausages. Drive to the summit of Fóia (902m, the highest point in the Algarve) for sweeping panoramic views over the mountains and coast.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the coast for a farewell evening at Praia da Marinha – watch the sunset from the clifftops, then a special last full dinner.

meals.breakfast: At the boutique stay
meals.lunch: Restaurante Central in Monchique town – hearty mountain food: carne de porco à alentejana, local sausages, and medronho; ~€15–22
meals.dinner: Restaurante Vale da Cova near Carvoeiro or a return visit to your favourite restaurant of the trip – make it a celebration dinner; ~€25–35 per person with a good bottle of Algarve wine

day_by_day.notes: The Serra de Monchique is dramatically different from the coast – cooler, greener, and very peaceful. Buy medronho (the local firewater) and smoked chouriço to take home. Fóia can be misty – check conditions before driving up.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning – one last swim at Praia da Marinha or a slow clifftop walk. Pack, check out of the boutique stay, and say goodbye to the limestone coast. Drive to Faro Airport (approximately 50 minutes), return the rental car, and allow 2 hours before departure.
day_by_day.afternoon: Departure from Faro Airport.
day_by_day.evening: Travel home with suntan, great memories, and a bag full of local wine and medronho.

meals.breakfast: Final breakfast at the boutique stay – linger over coffee and pastéis de nata
meals.lunch: Quick lunch at Faro Airport or a roadside café en route – prego no pão (steak sandwich) or a pastel de nata and espresso
meals.dinner: On the plane or at home

day_by_day.notes: Return rental car with a full tank of fuel – petrol stations are easy to find near the airport. Allow extra time if returning the car to a different location. Check in online the night before to save time. Faro Airport has a small but decent duty-free where you can pick up last-minute Portuguese wine, port, or Pastéis de Belém tins.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Portugal Algarve Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

hotel.name: Praia da Marinha, Lagoa Boutique Stay

experiences.name: Praia da Marinha Coastal Hike & Swim
experiences.description: Explore one of the Algarve's most stunning beaches, Praia da Marinha, known for its dramatic golden limestone cliffs, sea caves, and crystal-clear turquoise waters. Hike the clifftop trail for panoramic views, then descend to the secluded cove for a swim among the rock formations.

day_by_day.morning: N/A – Flight LH arrives at 13:00. Transfer from Faro Airport to Praia da Marinha, Lagoa Boutique Stay (~45 min private chauffeur transfer). Check-in, unpack, and settle into your luxury suite overlooking the Algarve coastline.
day_by_day.afternoon: After freshening up, take a leisurely stroll along the cliffs directly adjacent to Praia da Marinha. Admire the dramatic golden limestone rock formations, sea caves, and turquoise waters. A gentle introduction to the Algarve's natural beauty with no strenuous activity required after travel.
day_by_day.evening: Welcome dinner at a fine-dining restaurant in Lagoa or Carvoeiro – recommended: Vila Vita Parc's Ocean Restaurant (2 Michelin stars, ~20 min drive) or the intimate Bon Bon Restaurant in Carvoeiro (Michelin-starred). Enjoy a glass of local Algarve wine and fresh Atlantic seafood to celebrate your arrival.

meals.breakfast: N/A – in transit
meals.lunch: Light welcome spread arranged by the boutique stay upon arrival, or a charcuterie and cheese board at the hotel terrace
meals.dinner: Ocean Restaurant at Vila Vita Parc or Bon Bon, Carvoeiro – tasting menu with Algarve wine pairing (~€150–€250 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Pre-arrange private chauffeur transfer from Faro Airport. Request early check-in if possible. Keep Day 1 relaxed to recover from travel.

day_by_day.morning: Praia da Marinha Coastal Hike & Swim – Embark on the iconic cliff-top trail starting directly from the hotel. Explore secret grottos, hidden coves, and the famous rock arches. Descend to the beach for a morning swim in the crystal-clear water. The September sea temperature (~22°C) is perfect for swimming.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private boat tour departing from Benagil – sail along the stunning coastline, enter the legendary Benagil Sea Cave (Algar de Benagil), explore sea arches, and snorkel in secluded bays. Charter a private vessel for a fully bespoke experience (~3 hours).
day_by_day.evening: Sundowner cocktails on the hotel terrace watching the golden hour light play on the cliffs. Dinner at Restaurante Sueste in Ferragudo – a premium seafood restaurant on the river estuary known for its grilled fish and lobster, with beautiful waterfront views.

meals.breakfast: Full gourmet breakfast at the boutique stay – fresh pastries, local cheeses, smoked fish, seasonal fruit, and specialty coffee
meals.lunch: Picnic basket prepared by the hotel enjoyed on a secluded beach during the boat tour, or light bites at a clifftop café in Benagil
meals.dinner: Restaurante Sueste, Ferragudo – grilled sea bass, percebes (barnacles), and regional white wine (~€80–€120 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Book the private boat tour in advance through the hotel concierge. Bring reef-safe sunscreen, snorkel gear, and water shoes for the coastal hike.

day_by_day.morning: Drive west to Sagres and Cabo de São Vicente (~1.5 hours) – the southwestern tip of continental Europe. Visit the dramatic fortress (Fortaleza de Sagres), walk the windswept cliffs, and experience the raw, untamed beauty of this historic promontory where Portuguese explorers once set sail.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Praia do Beliche and Praia de Tonel near Sagres – quieter, wilder beaches with excellent surf and dramatic scenery. Alternatively, visit the Sagres Lighthouse and browse the small artisan market in Sagres village. Head back east, stopping at Salema or Burgau for a late afternoon beach walk.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner in Lagos – one of the Algarve's most vibrant towns (~30 min from the hotel). Recommended: Restaurante Adega da Marina (fresh cataplana dishes) or the upscale No Pátio for modern Portuguese cuisine in a charming courtyard setting.

meals.breakfast: Gourmet breakfast at the boutique stay
meals.lunch: Lunch at A Sagres or Restaurante O Telheiro do Infante in Sagres – fresh grilled fish with ocean views (~€40–€60 per person)
meals.dinner: No Pátio or Adega da Marina, Lagos – cataplana de marisco (seafood stew), local Alentejo wine (~€70–€100 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Rent a premium car (e.g., Mercedes GLC or similar) for the day trip. Sagres can be windy – bring a light jacket. September crowds are lighter than peak summer.

day_by_day.morning: Private wine tasting experience at Adega do Cantor (Sir Cliff Richard's winery) or Quinta dos Vales in Estômbar (~20 min from the hotel). Enjoy a guided tour of the vineyards, cellar, and a curated tasting of premium Algarve wines including their award-winning reds, whites, and rosés.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue to a second winery – Quinta da Penina or Herdade dos Grous (~45 min drive inland). Enjoy a wine and olive oil pairing lunch in a rural setting surrounded by vineyards and cork oak trees. Explore the estate grounds at leisure.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the hotel for a relaxing evening. Enjoy a private in-room or terrace dinner arranged by the boutique stay – a curated menu of local delicacies paired with wines from the day's tastings. Or opt for a quiet dinner at a nearby Carvoeiro restaurant such as Restaurante Valentim.

meals.breakfast: Gourmet breakfast at the boutique stay
meals.lunch: Wine and food pairing lunch at the winery estate – charcuterie, local cheeses, olives, and regional dishes (~€60–€90 per person, included in some premium tasting packages)
meals.dinner: Private terrace dinner at the boutique stay or Restaurante Valentim, Carvoeiro (~€60–€90 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Book wine tasting experiences at least 2–3 weeks in advance. Arrange a private driver for the day so both guests can fully enjoy the tastings without concern for driving.

day_by_day.morning: Relaxed beach morning at Praia da Marinha – set up with premium sun loungers and umbrellas (arranged by the hotel). Swim in the calm September sea, explore the rock pools, and enjoy the relative quiet of shoulder season. Optional: kayaking or paddleboarding along the base of the cliffs.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the charming hilltop village of Alte (~45 min drive north) – one of the Algarve's most picturesque inland villages. Stroll cobblestone streets, visit the 16th-century church, explore the natural spring and gardens, and browse local craft shops. A beautiful contrast to the coastal scenery.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner at Restaurante Casa do Prego in Silves or the acclaimed Madrugada in Armação de Pêra – a sophisticated seafood restaurant with panoramic ocean views and an excellent wine list. Watch the sunset over the Atlantic.

meals.breakfast: Gourmet breakfast at the boutique stay
meals.lunch: Lunch at a traditional tasca in Alte village – petiscos (Portuguese tapas), bifanas, and local craft beer (~€20–€35 per person)
meals.dinner: Madrugada, Armação de Pêra – fresh shellfish, grilled turbot, and premium Alentejo wine (~€80–€120 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Saturday evenings can be busier – book dinner reservations well in advance. The drive to Alte passes through beautiful Algarve countryside and cork forests.

day_by_day.morning: Private guided kayak and snorkel tour along the Praia da Marinha coastline – explore sea caves, hidden beaches, and underwater rock formations accessible only by water. A professional guide leads the 3-hour experience, with all premium equipment provided.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Silves – the historic Moorish capital of the Algarve (~30 min drive). Explore the magnificent red sandstone Castelo de Silves (castle), the Gothic cathedral, and the charming riverside town. Browse the Sunday market if still running and visit local artisan shops.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner in Silves at Marisqueira Rui – a legendary seafood restaurant beloved by locals and visitors alike, famous for its cataplana, grilled tiger prawns, and extensive wine cellar. A true Algarve institution.

meals.breakfast: Gourmet breakfast at the boutique stay
meals.lunch: Light lunch at a riverside café in Silves – fresh bread, local cheese, olives, and a glass of chilled Vinho Verde (~€25–€40 per person)
meals.dinner: Marisqueira Rui, Silves – cataplana de gambas, grilled lobster, and house white wine (~€70–€100 per person)

day_by_day.notes: The kayak tour should be booked through the hotel concierge. Wear water shoes and bring a dry bag for valuables. Silves castle is best visited in the afternoon when morning tour groups have cleared.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to the stunning beaches of the Alentejo coast – drive north to Comporta (~2.5 hours) or explore the wilder beaches near Odeceixe and Aljezur in Costa Vicentina Natural Park (~1 hour). These pristine, protected beaches offer dramatic scenery and far fewer crowds than the central Algarve.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Aljezur village – a charming whitewashed hilltop town with a Moorish castle, local market, and excellent sweet potato (batata-doce) specialties unique to the region. Walk the castle ruins for panoramic views over the surrounding countryside and coast.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the hotel and enjoy a spa evening – arrange an in-room massage or spa treatment through the boutique stay's concierge service. Light dinner at the hotel or a nearby Lagoa restaurant such as Restaurante Cantinho da Prainha.

meals.breakfast: Gourmet breakfast at the boutique stay – pack a gourmet picnic box for the day trip
meals.lunch: Gourmet picnic on Praia de Odeceixe or Praia da Amoreira – prepared by the hotel with local charcuterie, cheeses, wine, and pastries
meals.dinner: Light dinner at the hotel terrace or Cantinho da Prainha (~€50–€70 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Costa Vicentina is a protected natural park – no beach bars or facilities on many beaches. Pack everything you need. The drive through the Serra de Monchique foothills is spectacular.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Serra de Monchique – the lush mountain range inland from the Algarve (~1 hour drive). Hike to the summit of Fóia (902m), the highest point in southern Portugal, for sweeping panoramic views over the entire Algarve coastline and beyond. The September weather makes this ideal for hiking.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the charming spa town of Caldas de Monchique – a historic thermal spring village nestled in the valley. Visit the thermal baths, stroll the shaded gardens, browse artisan medronho (arbutus berry brandy) distilleries, and enjoy the cooler mountain air.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner at Restaurante Central de Monchique or O Parque in Caldas de Monchique – traditional mountain cuisine featuring piri-piri chicken, black pork (porco preto), and local honey cake (bolo de mel), paired with house-distilled medronho.

meals.breakfast: Gourmet breakfast at the boutique stay
meals.lunch: Lunch at a mountain restaurant in Monchique – carne de porco preto (black pork), migas, and local wine (~€35–€55 per person)
meals.dinner: O Parque, Caldas de Monchique – traditional Algarve mountain fare with medronho tasting (~€50–€70 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Wear comfortable hiking shoes for the Fóia summit trail. The mountain road to Monchique is winding – drive carefully. Purchase artisan medronho and honey as gifts or souvenirs.

day_by_day.morning: Private premium wine tasting at Herdade da Malhadinha Nova (~1 hour drive into Alentejo) – one of Portugal's most prestigious wine estates. Enjoy a private cellar tour, vineyard walk, and curated tasting of their acclaimed red wines, olive oils, and charcuterie in a stunning rural setting.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring the Alentejo landscape – visit the medieval walled city of Évora (~2 hours from the hotel, or plan as a full-day excursion). Alternatively, explore Beja or the beautiful cork oak forests (montado) of the Alentejo plains. Return via scenic countryside roads.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the hotel. Relaxed dinner at a top Carvoeiro restaurant – recommended: Restaurante O Castelo or the sophisticated Fortaleza do Beliche-style dining. Enjoy a digestif of aged Alentejo brandy on the hotel terrace under the stars.

meals.breakfast: Gourmet breakfast at the boutique stay
meals.lunch: Estate lunch at Herdade da Malhadinha Nova – premium wine and food pairing with regional Alentejo dishes (~€80–€120 per person, book in advance)
meals.dinner: Restaurante O Castelo, Carvoeiro – grilled fish, octopus salad, and local wine (~€60–€90 per person)

day_by_day.notes: The Alentejo wine estate visit requires advance reservation and is best arranged as a private, exclusive experience. Consider hiring a driver for the full day.

day_by_day.morning: Relaxed morning at leisure – sleep in, enjoy a slow gourmet breakfast on the hotel terrace, and take a final morning swim at Praia da Marinha. This mid-trip rest day allows for recovery and spontaneous exploration.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Portimão and Ferragudo – visit the Museu de Portimão (excellent maritime and canning history museum, free entry), walk across the historic bridge to the charming fishing village of Ferragudo, and browse its colorful streets and castle viewpoint.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails at a clifftop bar in Alvor or Praia da Rocha. Dinner at Restaurante Titanic in Portimão – a long-standing premium seafood institution known for its grilled fish, shellfish rice, and extensive wine list.

meals.breakfast: Extended gourmet breakfast at the boutique stay – take your time
meals.lunch: Lunch at Tasca do Celso in Ferragudo – a beloved local spot with fresh grilled fish and petiscos (~€35–€55 per person)
meals.dinner: Restaurante Titanic, Portimão – shellfish rice, grilled turbot, and premium Portuguese wine (~€70–€100 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Ferragudo is one of the most authentic and photogenic fishing villages in the Algarve – allow time to wander without a fixed schedule.

day_by_day.morning: Drive east to Tavira (~1.5 hours) – widely considered the most beautiful and romantic town in the Algarve. Explore the Roman bridge, Moorish castle, 37 historic churches, and the charming riverside market. Take the ferry to Ilha de Tavira – a pristine barrier island beach within the Ria Formosa Natural Park.
day_by_day.afternoon: Spend the afternoon on Ilha de Tavira – a long, unspoiled sandy beach with calm lagoon waters on one side and Atlantic waves on the other. Swim, sunbathe, and enjoy the natural beauty of this protected coastal ecosystem. Return by ferry to Tavira town.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner in Tavira – recommended: Restaurante Quatro Águas on the Ria Formosa lagoon, or the acclaimed Ponto de Encontro for traditional Algarve cuisine. Enjoy the magical evening atmosphere of this beautiful town before the drive back.

meals.breakfast: Gourmet breakfast at the boutique stay
meals.lunch: Fresh seafood lunch at a beach restaurant on Ilha de Tavira – grilled fish, clams, and chilled Vinho Verde (~€40–€60 per person)
meals.dinner: Quatro Águas, Tavira – fresh oysters from the Ria Formosa, grilled sea bream, and local wine (~€70–€100 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Tavira is a full day excursion – depart by 9:00 AM to maximize time. The Ria Formosa is a UNESCO-recognized biosphere – respect the natural environment. Book dinner in Tavira before departing.

day_by_day.morning: Final full beach day at Praia da Marinha and neighboring Praia de Benagil – savor the stunning scenery one last time. Rent a stand-up paddleboard and explore the coastline at your own pace, or simply relax on the golden sands with a good book.
day_by_day.afternoon: Premium spa afternoon at Vila Vita Parc Resort (~20 min drive) – enjoy access to their world-class spa facilities including indoor pool, steam room, and treatments. Book a couples massage or signature Algarve orange blossom treatment. Alternatively, enjoy a final wine tasting at a local Lagoa adega (wine cellar).
day_by_day.evening: Grand farewell dinner at the finest restaurant of the trip – Vila Vita Parc's Ocean Restaurant (2 Michelin stars) or Bon Bon (Michelin star) in Carvoeiro. Order the full tasting menu with premium wine pairing. Toast to an unforgettable Algarve experience.

meals.breakfast: Gourmet breakfast at the boutique stay
meals.lunch: Light beach lunch – fresh fruit, sandwiches, and sparkling water from a beachside café or hotel-prepared picnic
meals.dinner: Ocean Restaurant, Vila Vita Parc – 10-course tasting menu with Portuguese wine pairing (~€250–€350 per person). Reserve weeks in advance.

day_by_day.notes: This is the final full day – make it memorable. Book the Michelin-starred dinner reservation as early as possible in the trip planning process. Pack non-essential items in the evening to ease the next morning's departure.

day_by_day.morning: Final leisurely breakfast on the hotel terrace overlooking the Algarve cliffs. Take a last short walk to the clifftop viewpoint above Praia da Marinha for a farewell look at the stunning coastline. Check out of the boutique stay and load luggage into the private transfer vehicle.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private chauffeur transfer to Faro Airport (~45 min). Depending on flight time, stop in Faro town for a final coffee and pastel de nata at a local café, or browse the boutique shops in the historic old town near the cathedral. Faro's walled old town is charming and worth a brief visit.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Faro Airport. Carry home bottles of premium Algarve and Alentejo wines, artisan medronho, local honey, fleur de sel (sea salt), and memories of an extraordinary 13-day Algarve experience.

meals.breakfast: Final gourmet breakfast at the boutique stay – savor every bite
meals.lunch: Light lunch or snacks at Faro Airport or a café in Faro old town – pastel de nata, fresh orange juice, and a bica (espresso)
meals.dinner: In-flight or at destination

day_by_day.notes: Arrange private chauffeur return transfer in advance. Confirm flight check-in requirements and arrive at Faro Airport at least 2 hours before departure. Purchase any remaining gifts or wine at the airport duty-free or in Faro town.

query: Portugal Algarve, $2200, beach holiday with wine tasting, September 2026 from London
